recognize_zh: 大腸鏡影像可見一顆表面光滑、粉紅色、黏膜完整且有細小血管紋路的圓形隆起性息肉（polypoid lesion）；外觀屬黏膜下隆起型，本身無法判定為淋巴瘤，需靠切片確診。
features: Endoscopic view of colon (hepatic flexure) with a solitary, smooth, round polypoid lesion
Intact, glistening overlying mucosa with fine surface vascular pattern
No ulceration, surface erosion or irregular pit pattern visible
Surrounding haustral folds unremarkable with residual stool fluid
describe_en: Colonoscopic image shows a solitary, well-circumscribed, smooth, pink polypoid lesion at the hepatic flexure. The overlying mucosa appears intact without ulceration or an irregular surface pattern, suggesting a subepithelial or lymphoid-rich mass rather than an adenoma. The endoscopic appearance is nonspecific and cannot establish lymphoma. Histologic sampling is required; in this case the lesion proved to be follicular lymphoma, grade 1.

ddx.vs: Adenomas have a lobulated, reddish surface with an altered pit/glandular pattern, whereas this lesion has smooth normal-appearing mucosa over a submucosal bulge.
Lipomas are yellowish, soft and show the cushion (pillow) sign on probing, unlike this pink lesion; histology or EUS separates them.
Endoscopy cannot separate these; histology showing polarized reactive germinal centers and BCL2-negative follicles excludes lymphoma.
Colonic NETs are typically small yellowish submucosal nodules; distinction relies on biopsy with chromogranin/synaptophysin.
